queueProposal.problem: All 132 existing home_services businesses are service_area providers. The physical-premises matrix correctly has zero offices, but treating those zeros as an office acquisition queue does not measure customer choice for home visits.

ledgers.name: physicalPremisesIds
ledgers.meaning: Unique approved premises with sourced exact neighborhood and a real service in the category. Existing physical-coverage counts remain unchanged.

ledgers.name: verifiedVisitProviderIds
ledgers.meaning: Unique approved providers with an explicitly reviewed first-party claim of serving this exact neighborhood, or an explicit Sofia-wide home-visit claim covering it. The existing locationKind or cityCode alone is insufficient.
requiredEvidence: scope type: exact neighborhood or explicit Sofia-wide coverage
ledgers.unknownCoverage: Leave unknown; do not count a generic service_area record automatically in 97 neighborhoods.

queueProposal.effectiveOptions: Cardinality of the union of physicalPremisesIds and verifiedVisitProviderIds for one neighborhood/category. One provider ID counts once; a citywide provider is not cloned into multiple catalogue records. Preserve the physical and visiting subtotals separately.
dispatch: Lowest verified effective-options count first, then lowest neighborhood coverage and scarcest relevant category; stable alphabetical ties.
For home_visit-only categories, send the gap to a service-area evidence review queue, not a request to invent local offices.

Maintain a separate address/neighborhood-resolution queue for the 592 current premises without a neighborhood and 34 with unresolved broad areas. Resolve from authoritative source addresses rather than assigning guessed quarter centroids.
Unknown visiting coverage does not become zero confirmed supply or false citywide coverage. Keep its evidence status explicit.
No public filtering, ranking, taxonomy or service-area semantics change is authorized by this proposal.
